searchText: I'm sure Grandine emit `payload_attestation` SSE, but the spec expect `payload_attestation_message` as the topic. that could explain we are missing the event in the metric Hello <@680234424037670912>, while inspecting Teku's `head_v2` emission path I noticed that `head` and `head_v2` events are logically bundled together - which results in a duplicate v1 `head` emission when the head's payload status changes. https://github.com/Consensys/teku/blob/c905b16ae7f08634793f318442b5c0cbea2d41d3/data/beaconrestapi/src/main/java/tech/pegasys/teku/beaconrestapi/handlers/v1/events/EventSubscriptionManager.java#L142-L190 I'm working on the `head_v2` implementation in Lodestar, which is why I was taking a look at your implementation. putting here the `head_v2` implementation question for Teku & Prysm so it doesn't get lost we should only emit `head_v2` when head's payload status change from `empty` to `full`. however, should we emit the event as well when payload status change from `full` to `empty`? e.g. when payload got reorg I think that Teku already emits a new event on every payload status change. I suppose that these events will be helpful to the builder entity more than the VCs. If that is the behavior we want then beacon-APIs description of head_v2 should get updated accordingly. the only way a payload can be reorged is by the next beacon block, meaning the head would change, imo it's questionable to me to even have the `payload_status` as part of the event at all, but I would like to hear more opinions why this is useful, and also how others have implemented this <@921369499733725205> is representing lodestar on this matter, he started working on an implementation that'll be my bad, i probably wasn't fully across the subtlety there i'll read up and see whats expected iirc, if its firing twice then its changed its head - we've got two fork choice nodes so the head literally changes so maybe its just how it is... has anyone implemented that differently? Well, the only other available implementation atm is Prysm's. From what I've seen, they emit both events on head update, but only `head_v2` on payload import - which makes sense because head v1 can't reflect a payload status change anyways and that also prevents event duplication. doesnt that mean head is incorrect any time the payload doesnt arrive? that doesnt sound correct either the prysm behavior is definitley wrong if that's how it works starting to seem pointless having this v2 at all so the main point was the dependent root meaning changes https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/pull/590/changes so this whole discussion about payload available isn't really why it was even introduced but also from description `The node may emit a second head event for the same beacon block and slot if there is an update in the `payload_status` from empty to full.` so, it seems like its fine to emit both like teku does also to <@498331483732312075>'s point about the payload reorg, maybe he meant the following, you have `(B1, EMPTY)` and `(B1, FULL)`, then `get_head` for slot 1 would be `(B1, FULL)`, and for slot 2 `get_head` would be based on `should_extend_payload`, let's assume attsters vote for `(B1, EMPTY)` and slot 2 had no block, so in slot 3 `get_head` would be `(B1, EMPTY)` so the head flipped from `FULL` to `EMPTY` that is a reorg, but in regard to the `head` event, I don't think we would trigger that if we wanna match our current head (v1) emit pattern so based on that pr, yes theres a fair point that the dependent root meaning is fundamentally different - so v2 is important. yes, that confuses me too, who and for what do we consume it, I doubt there is any usage from the vc side, at least right now I don't see it to me teku complies with that description but i dont know who would be consuming the payload status maybe a builder? dont know so for slot 1, before you receive the payload your head is `(B1, EMPTY)` then it changes to `(B1, FULL)` on payload import, but both nodes have 0 weight, so for current slot, what value does this bring that `execution_payload` not already solves? maybe <@523051247884959744> or <@602753420033785856> have opinions, to me its inconsequential but i could definitely be missing something there was an issue from potuz here https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/issues/609 the note worth pointing out is the following: > we trigger a payload event but there is no signal as whether this payload was timely or not. seems like potuz is saying this should consider timeliness, but just from the conversation I don't think that's what teku does, even if payload is untimely, you will emit the 2nd event since head still changes to `(B, FULL)` in current slot, is that right? i wonder if ptc is not timely but we build or something weird i wonder if theres 3... not sure we have a test case like that for the `head_v2` you mean? yeh if it re-emits if ptc is not timely and we saw a payload it'd have to emit again to say payload not present even though we might have seen it? this seems all kinds of messy anyway if the field isnt even needed so for any use case the vc has, the `payload_status` is definitely not needed I am not sure how to interpret this https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/issues/609, but `whether this payload was timely or not` is fair point, we don't have such a event, unless I am missing something

excerpts.author: hangleang
excerpts.content: I'm sure Grandine emit `payload_attestation` SSE, but the spec expect `payload_attestation_message` as the topic. that could explain we are missing the event in the metric

excerpts.author: lqzic
excerpts.content:
Hello <@680234424037670912>, while inspecting Teku's `head_v2` emission path I noticed that `head` and `head_v2` events are logically bundled together - which results in a duplicate v1 `head` emission when the head's payload status changes.
https://github.com/Consensys/teku/blob/c905b16ae7f08634793f318442b5c0cbea2d41d3/data/beaconrestapi/src/main/java/tech/pegasys/teku/beaconrestapi/handlers/v1/events/EventSubscriptionManager.java#L142-L190
I'm working on the `head_v2` implementation in Lodestar, which is why I was taking a look at your implementation.

excerpts.author: lqzic
excerpts.content: putting here the `head_v2` implementation question for Teku & Prysm so it doesn't get lost

excerpts.author: hangleang
excerpts.content: we should only emit `head_v2` when head's payload status change from `empty` to `full`.  however, should we emit the event as well when payload status change from `full` to `empty`?

excerpts.author: hangleang
excerpts.content: e.g. when payload got reorg

excerpts.author: lqzic
excerpts.content: I think that Teku already emits a new event on every payload status change. I suppose that these events will be helpful to the builder entity more than the VCs. If that is the behavior we want then beacon-APIs description of head_v2 should get updated accordingly.

excerpts.author: nflaig
excerpts.content: the only way a payload can be reorged is by the next beacon block, meaning the head would change, imo it's questionable to me to even have the `payload_status` as part of the event at all, but I would like to hear more opinions why this is useful, and also how others have implemented this
